title: Rabbi Shiyan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Acha’s student: in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:6, “Rabbi Shiyan taught before Rabbi Acha.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 7, beginning of halakhah 2: “Rabbi Shiyan said: Rabbi Acha’s eye ranged over the whole Torah and did not find it” (he searched the whole Torah for a place where “labors” is written and did not find it).

He is mentioned at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 3, and Eruvin 6:6. His precious saying remains to us in Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 3:3: “Rabbi Shiyan said: One who is appointed [judge] for money — one does not rise before him, one does not call him Rabbi, and the cloak upon him is like a donkey’s saddlecloth.” See also the entry Rabbi Ashyan.

notes.text: The first series is Jerusalem Talmud. The paid-appointment saying, refusal to call him Rabbi and donkey-saddlecloth comparison preserve the supplied negative clauses; no identity is inferred from the cross-reference.

Guggenheimer Bikkurim 3:3 directly names Shiyan and preserves the two refusals and donkey-saddlecloth comparison. The cross-reference to Ashyan is not an identity determination, and other chapter/halakhah occurrences remain separate.
